knowledge_point.title: Finding the Slope of the Tangent Line to a Product  at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
If a curve $C$ is given by $y=(x^{2} + 2 x + 3)\cdot (\sin{\left(x \right)})$, calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.

Slope $=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)=x^{2} + 2 x + 3$ and $v(x)=\sin{\left(x \right)}.$ Then, we have

$$
u'(x)=2 x + 2,\quad v'(x)=\cos{\left(x \right)}.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx} &=uv'(x)+vu'(x) \\ &=(x^{2} + 2 x + 3)\cdot (\cos{\left(x \right)})+(\sin{\left(x \right)})\cdot (2 x + 2) \\ &=x^{2} \cos{\left(x \right)} + 2 x \sin{\left(x \right)} + 2 x \cos{\left(x \right)} + 2 \sin{\left(x \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(x \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\left.\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\right|_{x=\frac{\pi}{4}} &=((\frac{\pi}{4})^{2} + 2 (\frac{\pi}{4}) + 3)\cdot (\cos{\left((\frac{\pi}{4}) \right)})+(\sin{\left((\frac{\pi}{4}) \right)})\cdot (2 (\frac{\pi}{4}) + 2) \\ &=(\frac{\pi^{2}}{16} + \frac{\pi}{2} + 3)\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})+(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})\cdot (\frac{\pi}{2} + 2) \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{2} \left(\pi^{2} + 16 \pi + 80\right)}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $\frac{\sqrt{2} \left(\pi^{2} + 16 \pi + 80\right)}{32}.$
